   Pursuant to section 610.123.4, RSMo, the court finds the petitioner in the above titled cause is entitled to
   expungement of the arrest records specified in the petition bringing this action and recorded pursuant to section
   43.503, RSMo.

   The court orders each agency named as defendants in the attached petition to expunge the arrest records specified in
   the petition in the manner provided in section 610.124, RSMo.

   The court finds:

        that the arrest of the petitioner in the case recorded pursuant to section 43.503, RSMo, identified above was
        based on false information; that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge to believe that
        the individual committed the offense; that no charges will be pursued as a result of the arrest; that the
        petitioner/subject of the arrest has no prior or subsequent misdemeanor or felony convictions; that the
        petitioner/subject did not receive a suspended imposition of sentence (SIS) for which the arrest was made or for
        any offense related to the arrest; and that no civil action is pending relating to the arrest or the records sought to
        be expunged.

        that the petitioner was arrested for, or was subsequently charged with, a misdemeanor offense of chapter 303 or
        any moving violation as the term “moving violation” is defined under section 302.010, RSMo, except for any

   Therefore, pursuant to section 610.123.4, RSMo, the court orders each agency identified in the petition to expunge

Missouri arrest record expungement guide
Before you proceed
Stop: the false-information ground always requires legal assistance before proceeding. Take this prepared packet and your own
account of what happened to a lawyer. LegalEase does not decide that the arrest was based on false information or that probable
cause is absent; the court must make those findings.

Arrange the three standard fingerprint cards described below first; they are required before filing, even though this packet can be
prepared now.

Your answers for personal and legal review
Your own account, reproduced for your lawyer and your review: The report said I took a parcel from 88 Example Lane. I told the
officer I was at work at 900 Synthetic Office Road at that time. My time record and the coworker who was with me support my
account. I believe the report identified the wrong person and that the officer relied on that identification when arresting me.

This is your account, not a finding that the information was false or that probable cause is absent. Do not treat this counsel
handoff as an entered finding or signed testimony.

Suspended imposition of sentence for this arrest or a related offense: No. Charges expected to be pursued from this arrest: No.
Intoxication-related offense: No. Civil action pending relating to this arrest: No.

Commercial driver license held at arrest: No. Operating a commercial motor vehicle at arrest: No. These are answers about the
time of arrest, not current status.

Any misdemeanor or felony conviction before or after this arrest: No. This answer is supplied for court or counsel review; it does

Your section 610.122 packet
Prepared for Jordan Lee Example for the civil division of the Circuit Court in Jackson County, Missouri. Review every prefilled fact
before filing. This packet concerns one arrest on 01/12/2023 by Kansas City Police Department.

CR145 is the petition. FI-05 is the confidential filing cover sheet, including all four official source pages and extra party pages as
needed. CR143 is included only because you indicated the receiving court requests a proposed order. No fee waiver was
requested. Keep these instructions separate from documents submitted to the court.

Confirm the selected basis and records
You selected the false-information branch: arrest based on false information; no probable cause now to believe you committed the
offense; no charges will be pursued; no related suspended imposition of sentence; and no related civil action pending. Review
each sworn statement in CR145.

Request the arrest or booking report and citation from the arresting agency. Obtain your fingerprint-based criminal-history record
from the Missouri State Highway Patrol to build and check the agency list; confirm its current search fees. If charges were filed on
the traffic ground, obtain certified dismissal, nolle-prosequi or acquittal records for every related charge from the court clerk.
Obtain any docket and accurate record-holder names and addresses. Verify the county where the arrest occurred, arrest date,
offense, citation, OCN if assigned, case number and court division. Stop and obtain legal assistance if your records contradict a
required statement; this packet does not decide eligibility.

Obtain three standard fingerprint cards before filing. Call a local police department or sheriff’s office to ask whether it takes
applicant fingerprint impressions for court expungement, can provide three cards in one visit, the current cost for each card,
whether cash is required, and what identification to bring. Start early. One card is filed with the court; one is sent by the clerk to
the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons; keep the third card. These cards differ from fingerprints for a
Highway Patrol criminal-history search, and you do not have to buy a criminal record merely to obtain them. The packet does not
fabricate the cards.

File CR145 with the clerk of the civil division of the circuit court for Jackson County, where the arrest occurred. Ask that clerk for
the current filing fee, payment method, required copies, filing method and local submission requirements. Do not substitute a
conviction-expungement form for this arrest route.

CR145 directs the clerk to issue a copy to the prosecutor, send a copy of the petition and fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal
Record Repository, and notify the prosecutor and every named official, agency or entity of the hearing. Supply complete
addresses, confirm issuance and notice procedures with the clerk, and retain filing/service receipts. No service or hearing is
certified as completed in this packet.

official, agency or other entity. Attend the scheduled hearing and bring the underlying records and copies. Calendar the actual
notice from the court; no hearing date or outcome is predicted.

no-prior-or-subsequent-convictions judicial finding that the April 2024 CR145 petition does not contain. Leave both judicial
findings unchecked. Ask the court or counsel to resolve that wording before tendering the proposed order; do not infer a
participant restriction, alter the court text or sign for the judge. The petition can be prepared without a requested proposed order.

Obtain legal assistance if any civil action exists or is contemplated relating to the arrest or records, including an insurance or
employment dispute; if commercial driver license status at arrest is uncertain; if the offense may involve intoxication-related traffic
or boating; or if chapter 303 or moving-violation classification is unclear.

Stop for legal assistance if any related offense was not nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted; if you received a suspended
imposition of sentence for this arrest or a related offense; if the prosecutor or an agency protests expungement; or if anyone
appeals under section 610.124.2.

Obtain legal assistance if no local agency will provide the fingerprint cards; if you are not a United States citizen or there may be
an immigration consequence; or if you need to know whether destruction means a record can never be found. The
false-information ground always requires legal assistance, even if no other stop applies.

Review and execute
Compare every prefilled name, address, birth date, Social Security number, driver license, arrest fact, case and defendant
against your records. FI-05 is confidential: submit it using the court’s confidential filing procedure; do not attach an unredacted
copy to public instructions. The case-type table identifies XG for expungement of criminal/arrest records.

Do not sign CR145 beforehand. Take identification and sign its sworn statement before the notary, judge or clerk authorized to
administer the oath. Leave new case number, court ORI, court assignments, court findings, dates, file stamps, judicial and
notarial signatures to their owners. Leave the signature and both address lines under it blank until personal completion before the
officer administering the oath.

The attached records checklist is part of these instructions: arrest/citation; criminal history; case and disposition documents if
charges were filed; complete record-holder/service addresses; fingerprint card; and financial records if requesting waiver.

File and provide notice
File CR145 with the clerk of the civil division of the circuit court for Jackson County, where the arrest occurred. Ask that clerk for
the current filing fee, payment method, required copies, filing method and local submission requirements. Do not substitute a
conviction-expungement form for this arrest route.

CR145 directs the clerk to issue a copy to the prosecutor, send a copy of the petition and fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal
Record Repository, and notify the prosecutor and every named official, agency or entity of the hearing. Supply complete
addresses, confirm issuance and notice procedures with the clerk, and retain filing/service receipts. No service or hearing is
certified as completed in this packet.

The court sets a hearing no sooner than thirty days (30 days) after filing the petition and gives reasonable notice to every named
official, agency or other entity. Attend the scheduled hearing and bring the underlying records and copies. Calendar the actual
notice from the court; no hearing date or outcome is predicted.

Conditional order and fee waiver
Use CR143 only if the receiving court requests this proposed form and confirms it is appropriate. Its October 2016 text contains a
no-prior-or-subsequent-convictions judicial finding that the April 2024 CR145 petition does not contain. Leave both judicial
findings unchecked. Ask the court or counsel to resolve that wording before tendering the proposed order; do not infer a

When self-help must stop
Obtain legal assistance if any civil action exists or is contemplated relating to the arrest or records, including an insurance or
employment dispute; if commercial driver license status at arrest is uncertain; if the offense may involve intoxication-related traffic
or boating; or if chapter 303 or moving-violation classification is unclear.

Stop for legal assistance if any related offense was not nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted; if you received a suspended
imposition of sentence for this arrest or a related offense; if the prosecutor or an agency protests expungement; or if anyone
appeals under section 610.124.2.

Obtain legal assistance if no local agency will provide the fingerprint cards; if you are not a United States citizen or there may be
an immigration consequence; or if you need to know whether destruction means a record can never be found. The
false-information ground always requires legal assistance, even if no other stop applies.
